rows.text: A prison deck whose lock pieces are also its clock. Alela turns every artifact and enchantment you cast into a 1/1 flier, so Moat, Propaganda, Rhystic Study and the signets are not durdle — each one is a body. You wall off the ground and win in the air, where nobody is allowed to follow.

guide.title: The commander and the token engine

rows.name: Alela, Artful Provocateur
rows.text: flying, deathtouch, lifelink on a 2/3, other Faeries get +1/+0, and every artifact or enchantment spell makes a 1/1 flying Faerie. Read the deck as "every noncreature spell is also a creature spell".

rows.name: Bitterblossom
rows.text: a Faerie every upkeep for one life, forever, off a one-mana enchantment. The best turn-one play in the deck.

rows.name: Bitterbloom Bearer
rows.text: the second Bitterblossom. You want to see one of the two early enough that the wall has bodies behind it.

rows.name: Anointed Procession
rows.text: doubles every Faerie, every Bitterblossom trigger, every Construct off Urza's Saga. With Bitterblossom out it is two free fliers a turn.

rows.name: Roaming Throne
rows.text: name Faerie. Alela's cast trigger doubles, and so does Bitterblossom's — the Throne is the single biggest multiplier in the deck.

rows.name: Court of Grace
rows.text: a flier every upkeep, and a 4/4 Angel instead while you hold the monarchy. The card draw from being monarch is what you were short on.

guide.title: The wall, and why it is one-sided

rows.name: Moat
rows.text: creatures without flying cannot attack. Your entire board flies. This is not a symmetrical stax piece — it is a wall with a door only you can use.

rows.name: Propaganda
rows.text: taxes the fliers and the trample that Moat does not stop. In a four-player pod the tax is a deterrent: they go hit whoever did not pay for one.

rows.name: No Mercy
rows.text: anything that does connect with you dies. Between this and Moat, attacking you is a losing trade even before the tax.

rows.name: Authority of the Consuls
rows.text: everything they play arrives tapped, so no surprise blocker and no haste kill. It is also an enchantment, so it makes a Faerie.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: the same effect plus extort, and it turns off haste-based combo turns.

rows.name: Cursed Totem
rows.text: no creature activated abilities. Mana dorks, sac outlets and tutor creatures all stop. Your Faeries have no abilities to lose.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: in a deck already taxing their mana with Propaganda and Blind Obedience, the "unless they pay" cards get paid far less often. Alela makes a Faerie when you cast it.

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the early-game version. Cast it turn one or two and let the cumulative upkeep run three or four turns.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: same tax, on a body, and it survives Moat's world because it never needs to attack.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: the mana that pays for everything else. Nobody pays the two when they are already paying Propaganda.

rows.name: Kindred Discovery
rows.text: name Faerie. Draw on every token that enters and every one that attacks. With Bitterblossom and Anointed Procession this is two to four cards a turn.

rows.name: Reconnaissance Mission
rows.text: a card for every Faerie that connects, and under Moat they all connect.

rows.name: Enduring Curiosity
rows.text: the same job on an enchantment creature that comes back once when it dies.

rows.name: Idol of Oblivion
rows.text: a token every turn already means a card every turn; late it makes a 10/10.

guide.title: Turning Faeries into cards and kills

rows.name: Skullclamp
rows.text: your tokens are 1/1s that Alela makes 2/1. Clamping one kills it and draws two. This is a mana sink that never runs out while Bitterblossom is on the table.

rows.name: Grave Pact
rows.text: now every clamped Faerie makes all three opponents sacrifice a creature. Draw two, wipe the pod's board, repeat. This is the deck's real engine and the reason to prioritize Skullclamp.

rows.name: Braids, Arisen Nightmare
rows.text: feed her the same expendable Faeries, plus the Seals you have already used. Each one is draw a card and drain two, or they give up a permanent.

rows.name: Urza's Saga
rows.text: makes its own Construct, then fetches Skullclamp, Sol Ring or Mox Opal. Hall of Heliod's Generosity and Academy Ruins buy back what gets destroyed.

rows.name: Gravitational Shift
rows.text: fliers get +2/+0, everything on the ground gets -2/-0. Your Faeries become 4/1s and half the table's creatures shrink out of relevance. Combined with Moat this ends games in two swings.

rows.name: Sephara, Sky's Blade
rows.text: costs almost nothing with a board of fliers and gives them all lifelink and indestructible — the anti-wrath button and a damage doubler at once.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: the finisher. On a wide flying board, protection from creatures for the alpha strike or double strike for the kill, and both halves are on one card.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: the other way games end. Overload it once the wall is up and swing into an empty table.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: the counterspell you want most, because the floating mana deploys two prison pieces the following turn.

rows.name: Swan Song
rows.text: it gives them a 2/2 flier, which Moat does not stop — but Gravitational Shift shrinks it and No Mercy kills it if it ever attacks.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: for the one creature that flies or ignores Moat.

rows.name: Oubliette
rows.text: the cleanest answer to a commander, since it is not destruction, exile or targeting once it resolves.

rows.name: Imprisoned in the Moon
rows.text: turns a commander into a land they cannot recast from the command zone.

rows.name: Darksteel Mutation
rows.text: same idea for one mana, and it is an enchantment, so it makes a Faerie.

rows.name: Seal of Cleansing
rows.text: pre-pay for the artifact or enchantment removal, then crack it in response — and it is Braids food afterwards.

rows.name: Aura of Silence
rows.text: taxes their artifacts and enchantments two while it sits there, then eats one.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a hand that does two of these three things: makes mana, makes a Faerie every turn, and stops the fastest deck at the table. Bitterblossom plus any two lands is a keep on its own.

Alela does NOT need to come down on turn four. She is a value multiplier, not the plan — deploying Moat or Bitterblossom on curve matters more, and she is much safer cast into an untapped-mana table that is busy paying Propaganda.

rows.name: Moat
rows.text: hold it until a creature deck actually commits. Cast into an empty board it just eats a Krosan Grip for nothing.

rows.name: Skullclamp
rows.text: find this before you find a finisher. Clamp plus Bitterblossom plus Grave Pact is a better win condition than any single card in the deck.
